title: Work built for brands with a young audience
lede: A mix of Crow Loop Studio case studies and reference work from before the studio existed — clearly labeled, always.
inProductionNote: New Crow Loop Studio projects are currently in production — check back soon. Everything below is reference work from before the studio's official 01.09.2026 launch.

caseStudy.framingNote: A note on the numbers: these are kids'-audience placements, so there's no funnel or retargeting data. "Most-played" is the platform's own ranking, not a marketing metric — I'd rather say that plainly than dress it up.

ghostbusters.name: Ghostbusters – Haunted Mansion
ghostbusters.description: A cooperative ghost hunt with a competitive layer on top, built for Playmobil's Ghostbusters line.
ghostbusters.challenge: The client wanted a competitive action game — that's what resonates with the target audience of boys around age 10. But the IP itself is built on teamwork: Ghostbusters hunt as a team, not against each other.
ghostbusters.decision: I designed cooperative ghost-hunting with a competitive layer on top: players hunt together, but compete over who catches the most ghosts. This keeps the competition between players while staying true to the brand's story — the Ghostbusters hunt ghosts, not each other.
ghostbusters.outcome: Top 10 most-played games of the week on Toggo. It performed well enough that the client commissioned a second version reusing the same core mechanic, reskinned with Alvin and the Chipmunks — proof the mechanic had value beyond the original IP.

ciniMini.name: Cini Mini – Pyramide
ciniMini.description: A stacking game that turns Cini Mini's established mischief into the core obstacle.
ciniMini.challenge: How do you use more than a brand's art and name? Cini Mini's characters are established in TV and print advertising as rascals who lick and bite each other — I wanted to actually build that personality into the gameplay, not just skin a generic game with it.
ciniMini.decision: A stacking game where players build a pyramid of Cini Mini characters while managing the characters' own mischief — licking each other, causing the stack to collapse — as the core obstacle. The brand's personality trait is the mechanic, not decoration on top of one.
ciniMini.outcome: The game ran as a microsite tied to a limited ad flight and went offline after about a month, so there's no ranking data to point to. This one rests on the design decision itself rather than a metric — which is fine, and worth saying honestly.

idefix.name: Idefix – Vorsicht Römer
idefix.description: Every character from the Toggo spin-off gets a functional reason to exist in the game.
idefix.challenge: Built for the launch of a Toggo spin-off show, for a younger audience than the other two case studies. The game needed to showcase every character from the show while staying non-violent — Idefix and friends evade Roman patrols using cleverness, not combat.
idefix.decision: Each character's distinct ability becomes a way to outsmart the patrols, giving every cast member a functional reason to exist in the game rather than a cosmetic cameo.
idefix.outcome: Top 10 most-played games of the week on Toggo, with the longest streak of the three case studies here.
